Your digital product checkout is more than a payment button. 👀 If you sell ebooks, templates, courses, guides, Canva templates, or other digital products, you need to think about what happens after someone clicks “buy.” Before selling your first digital product, make sure you have: 1️⃣ Purchase terms — what the customer is actually agreeing to when they buy. 2️⃣ License & use restrictions — what they can and cannot do with your product. 3️⃣ Privacy Policy — especially if you’re collecting customer information. 4️⃣ Website/store terms — the rules governing purchases and use of your store. 5️⃣ Protection against unauthorized sharing & reselling — because your digital product should not become the internet’s free download. 😭 Your creativity is an asset. Treat it like one. And remember: your legal protection shouldn’t start after someone steals or misuses your digital product. It should be part of your business from the beginning. Digital products helped me turn my knowledge into passive income 💻💰 Now I’m showing other women how to do the same. 📈✨

Hear me out. 😂 When you’re creating your first digital product, it’s tempting to think it needs to do something HUGE. “Help women completely transform their finances.” “Teach someone everything about gardening.” “Show beginners everything they need to know about Canva.” But huge problems usually create huge products. And huge products can leave a beginner sitting there thinking: Where do I even START? I’d rather see you solve one small, specific problem really well. Instead of: Teach people gardening Try: Help a first-time gardener figure out what vegetables to plant in a small raised bed. That could become a simple raised-bed planting guide. Instead of: Teach people Canva Try: Help a small-business owner create her first branded Instagram post. That could become a simple Canva template pack with instructions. Smaller problem. Clearer buyer. Simpler product. And it’s much easier for the person seeing it to understand: “Oh. That’s for me.” You don’t have to solve someone’s entire life with your first digital product. You need to help with one problem they actually want solved. Not sure what your one thing could be?
